proof.note: Proof runs on the author's machine, 2026-11-02. Whisper ran on the CPU (int8): this box's CTranslate2 is built for CUDA 12 and its venv carries CUDA 13, so it can't use the card here and no VRAM was used.

captions.title: A voice-over on a silent clip
captions.alt: A cardboard robot in a beret sits in a director's chair beside a toy film camera. White captions with a black edge read: This little robot directs every shot.
captions.heard: This little robot directs every shot. Whisper wrote these words down, and FFM peg drew them in a real font.
captions.measured: Whisper's words were compared with the script by a program, and each caption card was read back off the burned frames by Tesseract OCR. The audio track was checked byte for byte against the source. Nobody has listened to it.
captions.script: This little robot directs every shot. Whisper wrote these words down, and ffmpeg drew them in a real font.
captions.voice: Kokoro am_michael, a built-in synthetic voice
captions.picture: An LTX-2.5 clip made in this studio, silent
captions.fault: Whisper wrote ffmpeg as "FFM peg", so one word in the captions is wrong and was split across two cards.

captions_more.title: MiniMax H3's own talking
captions_more.alt: An invented woman in a camel sweater talks to camera. White captions on a dark box read: screens after 10, same wake time, cold.
captions_more.heard: So I have you on a wait moment here, no screens after 10, same wake time, cold, dark room.
captions_more.measured: Whisper's words were compared with the script by a program, and each caption card was read back off the burned frames by Tesseract OCR. The audio track was checked byte for byte against the source. Nobody has listened to it.
captions_more.voice: Speech MiniMax H3 made with the picture
captions_more.picture: A MiniMax H3 clip of an invented adult, made in this studio
captions_more.fault: H3's speech is unclear in places, and the captions say what Whisper heard there ("So I have you on a wait moment here"). There is no script to score it against.

sound.title: Waves on rocks, sound from the picture alone
sound.alt: Waves break against dark rocks at sunset, throwing white spray up the cliff.
sound.picture: A Wan clip from this studio's showcase, silent
sound.measured: The sound was measured by programs: loudness by ffmpeg's EBU R128 filter, onsets and motion by librosa and frame differences, sync by cross-correlation against 2000 randomly shifted copies. Nobody has listened to it.
sound.fault: No measurable sync. The sound is a steady surf wash: the strongest sound near each splash (4.29, 4.63 and 4.92 s) is only 1.5 to 1.9 times the clip's typical onset strength, at -200, +50 and -20 ms, and the whole-clip cross-correlation with the picture's motion (r 0.02) is what randomly shifted sound gets 90% of the time.

sound.title: A flambé with the cook removed (VOID), given sound
sound.alt: A pan flames up on a stove in a dark restaurant kitchen; the cook who held it has been removed from the shot.
sound.picture: This studio's VOID removal example, silent
sound.measured: The sound was measured by programs: loudness by ffmpeg's EBU R128 filter, onsets and motion by librosa and frame differences, sync by cross-correlation against 2000 randomly shifted copies. Nobody has listened to it.
sound.fault: As generated it was too loud and clipped (-12.4 LUFS, true peak +0.5 dBTP); the studio now levels it to -16.1 LUFS, -3.1 dBTP. Two flame flare-ups (3.67 and 4.08 s) have a strong sound within 7 ms, but over the whole clip the match with the picture's motion (r 0.04) is no better than randomly shifted sound (p 0.79).

proof.sound_note: ControlFoley ran on the author's machine on 2026-11-02 in its own ComfyUI process: bf16, 25 steps, seed 42, no words to steer it. Its weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 and its DFN5B encoder is Apple research-only: these samples are for non-commercial demonstration.
proof.sound_honest: Generated ambience for the whole clip. It doesn't place sounds on visible events (measured: no better than chance).
